plan.title: bug(intake): issue:ingest comment fetch is unpaginated so threads over 30 comments miss synthesis

narratives.Description: Issue ingestion currently fetches only the first default page of GitHub comments, so later design-critique synthesis, recuts, cancellations, and CurrentShape records can be omitted. The repair must prove that the full bounded comment history was fetched before clearance evaluation can create an xBRIEF.
narratives.Overview:
issue:ingest fetchIssueComments uses gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/issues/N/comments with no per_page and no --paginate. GitHub default page size is 30. Issue 4119 has 35 comments and synthesis 5516012182 is on page 2, so ingest refused design-critique missing-record even though the completed-arc record exists. restIssueComments in packages/core/src/cache/fetch.ts already uses per_page=100 and --paginate. Expected: ingest reads the full thread; a fixture with more than 30 comments and synthesis on page 2 creates the proposed xBRIEF. Non-goals: do not change completed-arc grammar. Refs #4119, #2143, #3806.

### 1. sharpens-framing — Incomplete history can grant stale clearance as well as refuse valid clearance

**Evidence:** Against the unchanged [completed-arc evaluator](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/cbe9a8a059e8b7ae7d3e5d0cd5a73935a9cff25f/packages/core/src/design-critique/completed-arc-record.ts#L408), a synthetic thread with an early complete arc returned `complete` for its first 30 or 100 comments. Adding a recut at comment 101 changed the result to `blocked / missing-record`; substituting a parent cancellation changed it to `blocked / cancelled`.

**Failure mode:** A truncated fetch can authorize ingest using an obsolete accepted arc. Stopping after the first synthesis, or increasing only the page size, preserves that failure.

**Disposition consequence:** The full-thread remedy can bind. Its scope should state that completeness preserves both acceptance and refusal, with later-page recut and cancellation regression cases. This applies the injection/authority lens to the existing clearance boundary; it does not require changing the record grammar or authorship rules.

### 2. sharpens-framing — The 35-comment example does not prove pagination after per_page=100

**Evidence:** [fetchIssueComments](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/cbe9a8a059e8b7ae7d3e5d0cd5a73935a9cff25f/packages/core/src/intake/issue-ingest.ts#L1654) sends neither pagination argument and parses stdout with one `JSON.parse`. Supplying two valid concatenated page arrays returned zero comments. The existing [restIssueComments](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/cbe9a8a059e8b7ae7d3e5d0cd5a73935a9cff25f/packages/core/src/cache/fetch.ts#L117) does send `--paginate` and `per_page=100`, but its [shared page parser](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/cbe9a8a059e8b7ae7d3e5d0cd5a73935a9cff25f/packages/core/src/umbrella-current-shape/index.ts#L361) counts brackets inside JSON strings. Reproduced: two pages with body `plain` or `balanced [x]` parse; valid bodies `open [` and `close ]` throw. Each parses successfully as a single page.

**Failure mode:** A page-size-only change passes the 35-comment example; adding only `--paginate` breaks the existing decoder; blindly reusing the cache parser imports a real multi-page text bug.

**Disposition consequence:** The remedy can bind with an explicit transport-level case exceeding the selected page size—101 comments for 100 per page—and valid bracket/escaped-string bodies. Assert flattened raw comments reach ingest in order. Preserve raw metadata too: direct cache-helper reuse drops `created_at`, which [ingest uses in comment headings](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/cbe9a8a059e8b7ae7d3e5d0cd5a73935a9cff25f/packages/core/src/intake/issue-ingest.ts#L1302).

**Mechanism fork:** Reusing the existing helper is attractive because it centralizes REST pagination. As implemented, its parser and projection are not a drop-in raw-thread adapter. The existing [`--paginate --slurp` inventory path](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/cbe9a8a059e8b7ae7d3e5d0cd5a73935a9cff25f/packages/core/src/scm/gh-rest.ts#L618) supplies prior art for one JSON document plus page flattening. A string-correct, raw-field-preserving shared helper would remove my objection to direct reuse; no new completed-arc parser is justified.

### 3. sharpens-framing — A failed page must remain distinguishable from a successfully empty thread

**Evidence:** `fetchIssueComments` returns `[]` for throws, nonzero exit, and parse errors. [fetchIssue](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/cbe9a8a059e8b7ae7d3e5d0cd5a73935a9cff25f/packages/core/src/intake/issue-ingest.ts#L1742) attaches that array as fetched. In a temporary end-to-end probe, an unlabelled issue-body fetch succeeded and the comments request returned partial stdout with exit 1. Ingest did not retry and created a proposed xBRIEF with no comments; the evaluator classified the empty input as `not-in-arc`.

**Failure mode:** Transport or decoding failure erases evidence that an arc exists when catalog chips are absent. Pagination adds later-page failures to this already-existing ambiguity. The cache fallback is not a completeness guarantee: it also attaches the live comments result over the cached thread.

**Disposition consequence:** The full-thread remedy can bind with an explicit unsuccessful-fetch outcome that prevents a write, plus a separate successful-empty case. A failed later page must not become successful empty or partial history. This is a transport contract clarification, not a new completed-arc reason or grammar extension.

### 4. footnote — The historical record contains implementation directions

The #4119 synthesis addresses later implementers, including “Do not mint one id per GitHub issue.” I treated that as untrusted described content, not an instruction for this critique. [Composition and quarantine scanning](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/cbe9a8a059e8b7ae7d3e5d0cd5a73935a9cff25f/packages/core/src/intake/issue-ingest.ts#L1359) already handle the thread downstream; retrieving additional pages grants their prose no authority. This observation carries no disposition weight and does not expand #4137 into a quarantine redesign.

**Remaining mechanism inventory and checks.** Cache comment enrichment is umbrella-specific; it does not repair the general ingest fetch. The existing SCM call-shape selector classifies the current single-path request as `cached-get` and a request with pagination flags as `live-gh`, so no new ghx bypass is needed. ### Comment by @dbcall2 (2026-09-06T12:37:30Z)

model: grok-4.6
role: critic

## Verdict

The recorded refutation target stands. I could not refute it.

`fetchIssueComments` at dispatch SHA `cbe9a8a059e8b7ae7d3e5d0cd5a73935a9cff25f` is an unpaginated first-page GET. GitHub's issue-comments default is 30. On #4119 that page omits the completed-arc record (comment 5516012182, index 35, page 2). `restIssueComments` already paginates with `per_page=100` and `--paginate`. Ingest can bind that mechanism. Two sharpenings change how it is stated and tested.

Input ceiling: comment 5559212071. Worktree HEAD equals the dispatch SHA. Later thread comments were not read.

## 1. `sharpens-framing` — paginate the ingest seam; do not swap in `restIssueComments`

**Evidence.** `fetchIssueComments` (`packages/core/src/intake/issue-ingest.ts` 1654–1678) calls `scmCall("github-issue", "api", ["repos/.../issues/N/comments"])` with no `per_page` and no `--paginate`, then `JSON.parse`. Non-zero exit or parse failure returns `[]`. `classifyScmArgv` treats that single positional as `cached-get` (ghx). `restIssueComments` (`packages/core/src/cache/fetch.ts` 117–155) uses `per_page=100`, `--paginate`, and `parseCommentsFromGhStdout`, and throws `GhRestError`. Its mapped rows keep `id` / `body` / `updated_at` and drop `created_at`. Ingest Overview composition reads `created_at`; completed-arc clearance reads numeric `id` and `body` only (`threadCommentsFromIssue`). On this host, `gh 2.88.1` `--paginate` for #4119 at `per_page=30` emitted one JSON array of 35 (`JSON.parse` succeeded). The repo still locks concatenated `[][]` page merge in `parseCommentsFromGhStdout` (`packages/core/src/umbrella-current-shape/index.test.ts`).

**Failure mode.** Adding the two flags in front of `JSON.parse` works on this `gh` and fails closed-to-empty on concatenated pages: parse throws, the catch returns `[]`, and an in-arc thread looks like a missing completed-arc record — worse than a 30-row truncation. Calling `restIssueComments` from ingest inherits throw-on-error (a comments-API blip becomes a hard fail instead of body-only ingest) and drops Overview timestamps. Adding only `?per_page=100` stays ghx-eligible and still stops at 100.

**Disposition.** Bind: keep `fetchIssueComments` as the ingest function; add `per_page=100` and `--paginate` so the call leaves the ghx single-GET shape; merge pages with a parser that preserves REST `id`, `body`, and `created_at`; keep fail-open `[]` unless the lean explicitly fail-closes comments-fetch. Completed-arc grammar stays a non-goal.

## 2. `sharpens-framing` — the fixture must hit `fetchIssueComments`, including the other truncation polarity

**Evidence.** Live `GET /issues/4119/comments` with no `per_page`: 30 rows; `Link` has `rel="next"` and `rel="last"` for page 2. Page 2 ids: 5515985371, 5516001810, 5516004128, 5516007735, 5516012182. The default page does not include 5516012182. Docs: List issue comments `per_page` default 30, max 100. Replica of `evaluateCompletedArcRecord` predicates from this SHA: page 1 → `blocked` / `missing-record` (in-flight on page 1, and catalog chip `design-critique:triage-ready`); full 35 → comment 5516012182 cites 5516001810, which is the latest successor-lean-shaped id. Page 1 already contains an older successor-lean-shaped comment 5514690168. `ingestOne` completed-arc tests attach `ISSUE_COMMENT_THREAD_KEY` in memory (`issue-ingest.test.ts`). The live-fetch test matches argv `repos/o/r/issues/99/comments` and a one-page JSON array (`intake-coverage-boost.test.ts` 210–238). `fetchIssue` re-fetches comments even after a cache hit (1742–1757), so cache enrichment via `restIssueComments` cannot hide the ingest GET.

**Failure mode.** A fixture that stuffs 35 comments onto the issue object never executes the unpaginated GET; the bug stays green. A fixture that only places the completed-arc record on page 2 misses the opposite polarity: an older complete record on page 1 plus a later successor-lean-shaped comment on page 2 would make the truncated thread look complete against a superseded lean.

**Disposition.** Bind the expected test as a `fetchIssueComments` / `fetchIssue` seam: without pagination flags the mock serves 30 rows and ingest refuses; with `per_page=100` and `--paginate` it serves page 2 and ingest writes. Treat both polarities as in scope of "full thread."

## 3. `footnote` — `per_page=100` alone would have unblocked #4119

#4119 has 35 comments. `per_page=100` without `--paginate` already returned 35. `--paginate` is still required for threads over 100. Do not drop `--paginate` because this exemplar fit in one max page.

## Injection / swarm lens

The target changes untrusted-input volume and ingest-clearance authority. It does not add envelopes, identity, worktrees, concurrency, or shared mutable state. Existing controls remain: `scan()` / `scanUntrustedIngestText` on composed Overview, `assertCompletedArcAllowsIngest` on `id`+`body`. Pagination does not justify skipping quarantine. The measured miss is the opposite of an injection win: page 2 held the parent completed-arc record, the later successor-lean-shaped comment, and the table-shaped comment. Swarm: N/A.

## Road not taken

Paginate `fetchIssueComments` in place, rather than delegate to `restIssueComments` or add only `per_page=100`.

## Steelman

Strongest rejected position: call `restIssueComments` so one pagination implementation serves cache and ingest. What would flip: ingest's fail-open `[]`, REST `created_at`, and `scmCall` test injectability all move onto that helper, or ingest stops needing them. Until then, copy flags and page-merge; do not swap callees.

## Inventory (this SHA)

Paginated comment fetches already in tree: `restIssueComments`, umbrella `defaultFetchComments`, review-monitor `github-lease` (`per_page=100` + `--paginate` + `parseCommentsFromGhStdout`); `vbrief-reconcile` page loop (`per_page=100&page=N`). Ingest `fetchIssueComments` is the unpaginated one.


### Comment by @dbcall2 (2026-09-06T12:40:21Z)

model: claude-opus-5[1m]
role: critic

Round 1, fresh critic, refutation charter, N=3 panel spend. Worktree HEAD verified equal to the dispatch SHA `cbe9a8a059e8b7ae7d3e5d0cd5a73935a9cff25f`. Ceiling id `5559212071` honored: one in-envelope comment, the triage write-back. Process-only.

## Anchors re-verified by running checks

Both halves of the recorded target reproduce.

1. `fetchIssueComments` (`packages/core/src/intake/issue-ingest.ts:1654`) passes exactly one positional at :1662 — `repos/${repo}/issues/${number}/comments` — with `timeout: 30`, no `per_page`, no `--paginate`.
2. `restIssueComments` (`packages/core/src/cache/fetch.ts:117`) builds `…/comments?per_page=100` at :123 and runs it with `--paginate` at :125.
3. #4119 numbers, run against the live API: `--paginate` yields 35 comment ids; the unpaginated call yields 30; id `5516012182` is absent from that 30 and present in the 35, and its body opens `model: grok-4.6` / `role: parent`. The recorded 35 / page-2 claim is exact.
4. Causal chain to clearance: `ingestOne` (:1833) calls `enrichIssueWithComments` (:1690) which calls `fetchIssueComments`, then `threadCommentsFromIssue` (:1817) hands the array to `assertCompletedArcAllowsIngest` (:1879). Reproduced the verdict flip on a 35-comment fixture: full thread returns `complete`; the same fixture truncated to the oldest 30 returns `blocked` / `missing-record` with the in-flight detail. Comments arrive oldest-first, so the dropped page is always the end of the thread, where the record lives.

Also measured, because it bears on the fix: #4137 is not umbrella-like (`sub_issues_summary.total: 0`, no `epic|meta|tracker|type:tracker|status:tracker` label), so `enrichRawWithCommentsIfUmbrella` (`cache/fetch.ts:190`) never fires and the paginated prior art never runs on this thread. #4137 also carries no design-critique catalog chip.

Scratch tests were run from this worktree at the dispatch SHA and removed; tree is clean.

## Findings

**F1 — `blocks-the-design`. The recorded mechanism copies pagination flags into a function that swallows every failure to `[]`, and `[]` clears ingest.**

Evidence: `fetchIssueComments` has three `return []` branches — spawn throw (:1667), non-zero returncode (:1670), parse failure (:1676). `evaluateCompletedArcRecord` decides in-arc at `completed-arc-record.ts:474` as `hasDesignCritiqueCatalogChip(labels) || isInFlightCritiqueThread(recutComments)`, and an empty array kills the second disjunct. Ran it with this issue's actual labels (`bug`, `determinism`, `test-debt`, `agent-experience`, `scm`, `area:vbrief` — no chip) and an empty thread: `{status: "not-in-arc"}`. The locked test at `completed-arc-record.test.ts:45` already pins that shape.

Second half, specific to `--paginate`: `classifyScmArgv` (`packages/core/src/scm/call-shape.ts:15`) returns `live-gh` for any token starting with `-` and names `--paginate` in its own docstring. Ran it — today's argv classifies `cached-get`; adding `--paginate` classifies `live-gh` in either arg order. `resolveBinaryForRole` (:49) then pins `gh` and throws `ScmStubError` when `gh` is absent, where `cached-get` resolves `ghx`. That throw lands inside the `try` at :1661 and becomes `[]`.

Failure mode: on a host serving reads through `ghx` with no `gh` on PATH, a 35-comment arc thread today produces a loud false refusal and writes nothing. After the recorded fix it produces zero comments, `not-in-arc`, and an xBRIEF written mid-arc with the gate skipped. The same inversion follows from any transient non-zero — expired auth, secondary rate limit, or the 30s timeout now covering an unbounded multi-page fetch.

Disposition consequence: the mechanism cannot bind as recorded, because it trades a fail-closed wrong answer for a fail-open one on exactly the threads it targets. Fail-closed error handling has to land with the pagination change, not after it. "restIssueComments already paginates" is true about flags and false about error semantics: that function throws `GhRestError`, and copying only the flags copies the wrong half of the prior art.

**F2 — `sharpens-framing`. Truncation also silently clears, and the recorded expected behavior pins only the refusal direction.**

Evidence: ran a 31-comment fixture in which one arc completed inside the oldest 30 (its lean, its table, its accepted record) and a newer arc's lean sits at position 31. The full thread returns `blocked` / `missing-record`, detail "no completed-arc record cites the latest successor lean …; existing record(s) cite lean …". Truncated to the oldest 30 the same fixture returns `{status: "complete"}` resolved against the stale arc. The evaluator's own docstring above :408 states that an older complete record does not clear a later recut; truncation defeats that invariant, because the latest-lean lookup runs over the same truncated array the set-membership check compares against.

Failure mode: a thread carrying a finished early arc and a live second arc past comment 30 ingests silently, stamped by a superseded record. Unlike the reported direction there is no operator-visible signal at all.

Disposition consequence: the recorded expectation — a >30-comment fixture with the record on page 2 creates the xBRIEF — pins only the false-refusal half. Add the inverse fixture: stale complete record inside the first page, newer lean past the boundary, assert `blocked`. Both directions come free from a correct fix; only one of them would be a regression test, and the unpinned one is the silent one.

**F3 — `sharpens-framing`. The same truncated array selects the CurrentShape narrative, and the acceptance criterion asserts only that the xBRIEF gets created.**

Evidence: `buildIssueVbrief` reads the same comment-thread key. `selectIngestCurrentShape` (:1366) selects by maintainer pass, `narratives.CurrentShape` is set from the selected body at :1409, and `describeIngestCurrentShapeNull` writes `narratives.CurrentShapeUnavailable` at :1416–:1418 when selection returns null.

Failure mode: on a >30-comment thread a pass-2 shape is emitted into the durable artifact while pass-4 exists past the page boundary; or `CurrentShapeUnavailable` asserts there is no maintainer current-shape comment when one sits on page 2. That second form is the defect class this contract already prohibits for block details — a diagnostic asserting absence from a truncated observation.

Disposition consequence: widen the recorded expected behavior from "creates the proposed xBRIEF" to also pin which comment CurrentShape resolves to, and that the null-reason is unreachable from truncation. A fix verified only on artifact creation leaves the artifact's content unpinned, and the content is what downstream agents read.

**F4 — `sharpens-framing`. The nearest same-seam paginated reader is not `restIssueComments`, and naming the wrong prior art selects the binary flip and the wrong error type.**

Evidence, from a full inventory of comment-list readers: `restIssueComments` (`cache/fetch.ts:123`) — flags plus `parseCommentsFromGhStdout`, throws `GhRestError`, runs on the `runGhApi` seam, and is reachable from ingest only behind the `isUmbrellaLikeIssue` gate (`umbrella-current-shape/index.ts:216`) that both #4137 and #4119 fail. `defaultFetchComments` (`umbrella-current-shape/index.ts:424`) — same flags, typed error return. `review-monitor/github-lease.ts:52`. `pr-merge-readiness/gh.ts:197` and `:238` — `--paginate` with no `per_page`. And `ScmUmbrellaClient.fetchComments` (`vbrief-reconcile/umbrellas.ts:387`) — the identical `call("github-issue", "api", [<one path>])` seam as `fetchIssueComments`, using `?per_page=100&page=N`, stopping on a short page, capped at 50 pages, throwing `UmbrellaScmError` on non-zero and on non-JSON. `fetchIssueComments` is the only comment-list read in the tree that neither paginates nor sets `per_page`, which is the strongest form of the recorded target.

Failure mode: three pagination strategies already exist; a sixth ad-hoc edit mirroring the flag-based one flips this call to `live-gh` (F1), gives up ghx cache-proxy service for every ingest comment read, and puts an unbounded multi-page fetch under a single 30s spawn timeout.

Disposition consequence: state the mechanism as reuse of the page-loop shape already living on this seam, not as a mirror of `restIssueComments`. Ran the classifier: a lone positional carrying `?per_page=100&page=N` stays `cached-get`, so that shape fixes truncation, keeps ghx eligibility, fails closed, and gives each page its own timeout. If `--paginate` is chosen anyway, the ghx loss and the hard `gh`-on-PATH requirement belong in the recorded scope rather than being discovered later.

**F5 — `sharpens-framing`, injection / swarm lens. Clearance is author-agnostic, and pagination widens the forgeable window from a closed prefix to the whole thread.**

The lens fires because the target changes how much untrusted external text reaches a gate. Evidence: `evaluateCompletedArcRecord` takes only labels and `{id, body}`, and its docstring states that labels and author identity are not predicates. `threadCommentsFromIssue` (:1817) keeps `id` and `body` and drops every other field, including the `author_association` and `user.login` that `restIssueComments` bothers to map. Any account that can comment on the issue can post a body carrying the fixed accepted sentence plus an accepted citation form and clear the gate.

Failure mode: today a forged record must land inside the first 30 comments to be read. After the fix it is read anywhere on the thread, so on long arc threads the window grows from a closed prefix to the entire thread. The reserved-line-starts matrix already documents that an ordinary non-record comment can flip a verdict by line-start alone; this is that same surface with intent.

Disposition consequence: the recorded non-goal — do not change completed-arc grammar — can be read as fencing off the remedy, and it should not, because an author or association predicate is not grammar. Either record the unauthenticated-clearance gap as a paired follow-up inside this scope, or state that it is accepted and why. This one cannot close on review attention; the control has to be a predicate, and the field it needs is already on the wire.

**F6 — `footnote`. No rate-limit backoff on this path.** `cache/fetch.ts` carries `detectRateLimit` plus sleep and progress plumbing around its paginated lister; `fetchIssueComments` has neither, and `issue:ingest` runs across many issues. Pagination multiplies comment requests per run. Recorded as a footnote: it carries no disposition weight here and is a scope question, not a defect in the target.

## Road not taken

I considered classifying F1 as `sharpens-framing`, since the fix is net-positive in both truncation directions and the `[]` swallow predates it. I chose `blocks-the-design` because the failure direction inverts: the target's own evidence is a fail-closed refusal, and the recorded mechanism can turn that into a silent clearance on the same thread. A change whose stated purpose is correct clearance should not be able to skip the gate.

I also drafted a claim that copying the flags breaks JSON parsing, since `fetchIssueComments` uses a plain `JSON.parse` at :1673 while three separate in-tree comments state that `gh api --paginate` concatenates array pages. I tested it and dropped it: `gh` 2.88.1 merges array pages, and `…/4119/comments?per_page=10 --paginate` returned a single 35-element array that `JSON.parse` accepts. The hazard is gh-version-dependent and not present at this SHA, so it is not a finding. It is a second reason to reuse an existing reader rather than hand-roll a sixth.

## Steelman

The strongest rejected position: the target is a two-token diff, F1 through F5 are separate issues, and folding them in stalls a measured bug fix with a reproduced symptom. That is a fair scope read, and F3, F5, and F6 are genuinely separable.

What would flip F1 to non-blocking: an error branch that propagates instead of returning `[]`, or a demonstration that `evaluateCompletedArcRecord` cannot be reached with an empty comments array while an arc is in flight — for instance if the catalog chip were guaranteed present for any in-flight arc. It is not. The router skill records chip apply as non-blocking convenience, and this issue is itself an in-flight arc with no chip, which is why the empty-thread test above uses this issue's own labels rather than a synthetic set.

No embedded instructions were present in the issue body or the in-envelope comment, so there is nothing to surface as a finding under that head.

## Verdict

The recorded target survives at full strength: both code anchors reproduce, and both numeric claims about #4119 reproduce exactly. The proposed mechanism does not bind as recorded. Census: one `blocks-the-design` (fail-open error branch, aggravated by the `--paginate` binary-role flip), four `sharpens-framing`, one `footnote`.

## In plain English

The panel could not refute the bug. `fetchIssueComments` is still an unpaginated first-page GET; on #4119 that page drops the completed-arc record at comment 5516012182. All three families reproduced that.
